title: Ribbon categories and Reshetikhin–Turaev knot invariants

items.title: Colored framed-link evaluation from a ribbon category
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.
items.strategy: Uses the complete multicolored ribbon-tangle evaluator, checks that a closed link has empty boundary and that framed isotopy preserves its value, and distinguishes End_C(1) from a field scalar.

references.title: V. G. Turaev, Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds, Chapter I, Theorem 2.5 and §§3–4
P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§8.9–8.10

items.axiom_use: Uses countable choice only through the cited construction of the framed ribbon-tangle evaluator.

items.title: The fundamental quantum sl2 module in the Kauffman-bracket ribbon convention
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$. The parameter and Cartan-generator conversion from Korinman's convention is $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$; the root generators $E,F$ correspond unchanged. The vector basis order remains $(v_+,v_-)$. Korinman displays these same column-action matrices for the root generators; no transpose is required. Thus the module matrices are
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. The parameters $q_K$ and $q_L$ are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Korinman's §2.1 matrix
$$C_K=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix}$$
is labeled there as the matrix of his inverse half-ribbon operator on the underlying vector space $V$. It is not the equivariant left-duality identification used below. Here $\Omega$ denotes specifically the Snyder–Tingley operator $X$, whose inverse matrix is computed independently below; it is not identified with $C_K$.

To specify the half-ribbon action, use the Snyder–Tingley convention $q_{\mathrm{ST}}=q_K$, $K_{\mathrm{ST}}=K_K=K_L^{-1}$, $E_{\mathrm{ST}}=E$, and $F_{\mathrm{ST}}=F$ in the same ordered basis. Since $q_K=\omega^{-4}$, choose $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$. Let $X=JT_{w_0}$ be their half-ribbon element and let $\Omega$ be its operator on $V$. On the fundamental highest- and lowest-weight vectors, their formula gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. The half-ribbon action therefore gives the actual inverse matrix and its square:
$$\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Omega^2=-\omega^{-6}\operatorname{id}_V=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V.$$
Snyder–Tingley’s associated Hopf-algebra ribbon element is $X^{-2}$; the positive categorical twist in this Kauffman-bracket convention is its inverse $X^2=\Omega^2$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.
items.strategy: Checks the generator action and finite matrix identities in the fixed q-inverted Hopf convention; imports only the full-text half-ribbon existence theorem and records the Kauffman-bracket ribbon choice explicitly.

items.title: Ribbon evaluation from a colored braid word
items.statement:
An **effective field** is a field whose elements have finite encodings and whose exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality test, and inversion of nonzero elements are terminating procedures. Input a finite-dimensional strict matrix realization over an effective field $k$ of a $k$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$, finite-dimensional color objects with fixed bases, exact matrices for every braiding and inverse braiding used, the evaluation and coevaluation maps for the closure, the twist matrices, and the matrix $J_W$ of the ribbon-induced pivotal comparison $j_W=u_W\circ\theta_W:W\to W^{\vee\vee}$ for $W=V_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{a_n}$, where $u_W$ is the Drinfeld morphism. Also input a finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands and the top color tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The matrices are assumed to satisfy the stated ribbon-category axioms; an implementation does not infer those axioms from arbitrary matrices.

Use the strand-position permutation homomorphism $\pi:B_n\to\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $\pi(\sigma_i)=(i\ i+1)$. Read the braid letters in composition order, updating the current color tuple at each crossing by swapping its adjacent colors. For a positive letter $\sigma_i$, use the matrix of
$$1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}}\otimes\cdots\otimes1,$$
and for a negative letter $\sigma_i^{-1}$ use $1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_{i+1}},V_{a_i}}^{-1}\otimes\cdots\otimes1$, whose source adjacent factors are $V_{a_i}\otimes V_{a_{i+1}}$. Here the subscripts always refer to the current tuple before the swap. Let the blackboard-framed closure join the bottom and top endpoint at each position by the identity pairing. Reject the input if the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple: the tuple records the colors at the paired endpoints, so equality is exactly the condition that the closure carries a consistent color on every component. Starting with the identity matrix, multiply the typed crossing matrices in word order to obtain $M_\beta:W\to W$, then return the finite matrix contraction
$$\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}\bigl((J_WM_\beta)\otimes1_{W^\vee}\bigr)\operatorname{coev}_W\in k.$$
In ordinary dual-basis coordinates this contraction is the matrix trace $\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)$.
No algorithm is asserted for arbitrary abstract ribbon categories without effective finite matrix data.
items.strategy: Checks color preservation around permutation cycles, multiplies the typed positive or inverse braiding matrices in word order, and contracts the resulting endomorphism with the supplied pivotal trace matrices.

items.title: Framed colored-braid representative independence
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. If two finite colored braids have color-preserving endpoint permutations and their blackboard-framed closures are isotopic as oriented framed links by an isotopy preserving each component color, then their evaluations agree in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)$. Thus the framed colored evaluation of a closed braid is independent of its colored-braid representative whenever the represented framed colored links are the same.
items.strategy: Realizes each closure as a colored framed tangle, uses the verified mixed-orientation ribbon evaluator to compare its morphism under framed isotopy, and applies the closed-tangle evaluation definition.

items.title: Scalar twist correction removes the framing
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.
items.strategy: Proves conjugation invariance by categorical-trace cyclicity, cancels both Markov stabilization factors against the writhe change, and invokes Markov's theorem under the explicitly stated choice axiom.

items.title: Correctness and termination of the colored-braid evaluation procedure
items.statement: For every valid input of the colored-braid evaluation algorithm, where the braid word has $m$ letters and the total tensor-product dimension is $D$, the procedure terminates after exactly $m$ crossing-matrix updates and one finite pivotal-trace contraction. It returns the ribbon-category evaluation of that framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. The stated bound concerns the number of matrix updates; each update is a finite exact matrix multiplication over the effective field.
items.strategy: Bounds the iteration by the finite word length, proves each letter update is the represented braid generator or its inverse, and identifies the final matrix contraction with the categorical closure trace.

items.title: The fundamental quantum sl2 ribbon trace matches the Hecke and bracket evaluations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $q_K=A^2$, $q_L=A^{-2}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Use the fundamental module, positive crossing, duality maps, and twist fixed in the preceding definition. For every $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the categorical ribbon trace of its blackboard-framed closure and let $w(\beta)$ be its exponent sum. With $t=A^{-4}$ and $z_0=-1/(t+1)$, the exact identities are
$$t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle=\delta^n(-A)^{w(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\ z=z_0},$$
$$(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)=\delta(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}\langle\widehat\beta\rangle.$$
Here $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is the normalized type-A Hecke Markov trace with braid generator sent to $T_i$, and $\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$ is the Kauffman bracket in the fixed crossing chart. The second identity is a value-by-value normalization formula; it does not by itself assert a Jones-polynomial specialization.
items.strategy: Extracts the Temperley–Lieb generator from the explicit braiding matrix, verifies its loop and neighboring-generator relations, matches the categorical pivotal closure with the bracket closure, and then applies the Hecke–bracket trace dictionary and the exact scalar twist correction.

items.title: A decomposable color with nonscalar twist has no single writhe correction
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The counterexample uses the following category: objects are finite-dimensional rational vector spaces $U$ with a linear involution $S_U:U\to U$ satisfying $S_U^2=1_U$; morphisms $f:U\to W$ are rational-linear maps satisfying $fS_U=S_Wf$, with ordinary addition and scalar multiplication on each morphism space; tensor product has involution $S_U\otimes S_W$, the unit is $\mathbb Q$ with identity involution, and associators and unitors are the usual vector-space maps. The braiding is the ordinary flip $u\otimes w\mapsto w\otimes u$. The chosen left dual of $U$ is $U^*$ with involution $S_{U^*}=(S_U^{-1})^*$, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_U(f\otimes u)=f(u)$, and coevaluation $\operatorname{coev}_U(1)=\sum_i e_i\otimes e^i$ for any basis $(e_i)$ and its dual basis $(e^i)$. The twist is $\theta_U=S_U$. This is a $\mathbb Q$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$. For $X=\mathbb Qe_+\oplus\mathbb Qe_-$ with $S_X=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, the twist is invertible and nonscalar, its one-strand identity ribbon trace is $0$, and its positive two-strand stabilization ribbon trace is $2$. Therefore no nonzero scalar writhe correction works.
items.strategy: Computes the twist and two categorical traces on explicit bases and compares the closures using the positive Markov stabilization.
